last_test: The original memorial, no. 548983, confirms an assignment dated 31 May 1825 naming John Glasgow senior of Gortin, County Tyrone, farmer, and John Glasgow junior of Cookstown, grocer. Its recitals confirm junior’s £50 debt to senior and senior’s security for junior in two bonds totaling £150, secured by the mortgage of 16 March 1824. The final passage is witness testimony, not a father/son statement. The 45% possible-father hypothesis is unchanged: financial support and senior/junior descriptions support a family interpretation, while collateral kin or an unrelated creditor remain possible.
next_test: Locate the recited 16 March 1824 mortgage and test the two John identities against their holdings and families; seek an identifying kin clause. Original opening, recitals and final attestation are now checked; do not repeat the same image review.
conclusion: Original source pixels for the opening parties, financial recitals and closing attestation were inspected on 12 November 2026, DGS 008091900 images 36–38. This verifies selected material readings, not a complete diplomatic transcription; registration day, manuscript pagination, exact jurat date and uncertain witness placenames remain unasserted. No explicit father/son clause was found in the inspected deed passages. Both profile identities remain inferred. The older Gortin father must be distinct from John-1968 if the latter’s c1778 estimate is retained; a c1778 man cannot father the merchant with an estimated birth before 1788. The 1826 tithe source remains an index, original uninspected. John-2990 remains an unselected 15% alternative. No mother, merge, vital change or confident connection follows.
